purpose: Establish an explicit import-aware module graph beside the existing FrontendSession and ModuleStmt loading path without changing current semantic or artifact behavior.
question: What module identities and dependency edges must the import-aware frontend session expose before interface-driven semantics and separate compilation can begin?
decision: FrontendSession publishes a snapshot-local ModuleGraph after successful import-aware file loading. Nodes use the existing module IDs and record source identity, diagnostic display path, canonical duplicate-import path, and entry status. Edges preserve one source declaration per import or source-bearing re-export and point to resolved module IDs with an Import or ReExport kind and decoded requested path.

module_identity.module_id: The existing snapshot-local module ID shared by ModuleStmt, ImportStmt, and ExportStmt resolution metadata.
module_identity.assignment: Deterministic dependency-first load order for a fixed ordered root list, import search path list, and source contents.
module_identity.canonical_path: Normalized existing canonical path used for duplicate-import de-duplication and graph node identity within the session.
module_identity.display_path: The requested/display path retained for diagnostics and source-origin reporting; it is not the persistent identity.
module_identity.source_id: Snapshot-local SourceFileId for the original source text and source metadata.
module_identity.persistence: Module IDs, source IDs, and graph vectors are not serialized into cdbc artifacts or used as cross-build cache keys.

edge_contract.import: Every ImportStmt contributes one edge from its containing module to its resolved target.
edge_contract.re_export: Every ExportStmt with a source path contributes one ReExport edge; local export lists do not contribute dependency edges.
edge_contract.duplicate_imports: Repeated canonical imports reuse one target node while retaining one edge for each source declaration.
edge_contract.cycles: Existing deterministic cycle rejection runs during loading before graph publication and remains unchanged.
edge_contract.requested_path: The edge stores the decoded source path token, while endpoint identity uses the resolved canonical node.

compatibility_boundary.import_aware_files: Graph construction is active for file loads that use the import-aware path.
compatibility_boundary.direct_multi_file: Ordered direct multi-file inputs without imports remain one combined entry program and do not become graph nodes.
compatibility_boundary.stdin: Stdin loading retains its existing behavior and does not publish an import graph.
compatibility_boundary.consumers: TypeChecker, DeclarationIndex, IR, bytecode, module-interface emission, diagnostics, and the Rust VM continue to use their existing paths in this slice.

migration: Build the graph beside ParsedUnit and ModuleStmt assembly. Use focused FrontendSession assertions to compare node/edge references, source origins, re-export edges, and repeated equivalent loads. Later M3A slices will migrate visibility and interface consumers; M3B owns dependency-body lowering removal and incremental compilation.
quantitative_gate: The frontend_session CTest validates three nodes, three edges, exactly one entry node, complete source origins, all endpoint references, and field-for-field equality across equivalent search-path loads. The m0d-2026-07-22-r1 inventory validates 1,745 cases, and the canonical verification plus legacy parity commands report zero unexplained differences.
old_path_deletion_condition: Delete no production path in this slice. Graph-derived module identity may replace dependency-body lookup only after M3A interface and visibility consumers read graph nodes and edges without fallback AST-body reads; direct single-file, stdin, and ordered direct-multi-file adapters remain documented compatibility paths.
affected_consumers: ModuleStmt, ImportStmt, and ExportStmt resolved module IDs
source metadata and file-aware diagnostic origin mapping
future M3A interface and visibility consumers
out_of_scope: module-interface serialization and imported signature materialization
new cycle policy or cycle diagnostic format
separate compilation and incremental cache keys
per-module cdbc artifacts or graph persistence
changes to direct multi-file, stdin, diagnostics, IR, bytecode, or Rust VM behavior
